message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he played high school basketball at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he gained national attention and was named the USA Today High School Player of the Year. 

He entered the NBA directly from high school in 2003, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers. Over his career, LeBron has played for the Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers. He has won four NBA championships (2007, 2012, 2013, 2020), earned four NBA Most Valuable Player awards, and has been selected to numerous All‑NBA teams and All‑Star games.

Beyond the court, LeBron is known for his philanthropy—most notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I Promise” school in Akron—and for his ventures in entertainment, media, and business. He remains a prominent public figure, both for his athletic achievements and his influence on social and cultural issues.
